To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the coupling between visual input and locomotor output is necessary for the normal functional development of visual cortex.

1) the coupling between visual input and motor output is necessary for the normal functional development of visual cortical processing, 2) this experience-dependent functional development of visual cortex involves an increase of inhibitory input onto excitatory neurons and a decrease of the inhibitory input onto inhibitory neurons, and 3) this experience-dependent change of inhibition is driven by a transient increase of the inhibitory drive of somatostatin positive neurons onto both excitatory and inhibitiory neurons.
the coupling between locomotion and visual feedback is critical for the development of the neural circuits in mouse visual cortex that process visual feedback.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the brain processes information about the environment and controls the movements of our body.
how the brain develops its functional architecture during a critical period of development.
the mechanisms by which the nervous system learns to associate sensory inputs with motor outputs, which is a fundamental process for the development of sensory-guided behaviors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the coupling between visual feedback and motor output shapes the functional development of L2/3 V1 neurons.
visuomotor feedback is necessary for normal functional development of L2/3 in mouse V1.
visual cortex is shaped by visuomotoral coupling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the coupling between the motor output and the visual input shapes the functional development of mouse visual cortex.
the functional development of V1 is experience dependent and that visuomotor feedback is a major source of experience.
the coupling between sensory input and motor output shapes the functional development of primary sensory cortex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sensorimotor coupling is necessary to shape visual processing in the mouse visual cortex.
visuomotor learning shapes the functional development of the mouse visual cortex.
visuomotor integration during development shapes the function of visual cortical circuits.
